title: CLO7.3 New Features: AI-Generated Textures, Quick Editing of Multiple Panels... Comprehensive Updates to Upgrade Your Design Experience!
description:
Fill out the CLO7.3 user experience survey to help with future updates and upgrades of CLO → https://www.wjx.cn/vm/YQU8gu2.aspx#

Comprehensive explanation video of the new CLO7.3 version, featuring a new Fabric Generator, AI Texture Generator, and linked editing new functions, along with more feature upgrades to fully accelerate your design process and improve work efficiency!
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am Claude Andy. Today, Celia and I will explain the new features of version 7.3 for you.  
The new features mainly include six parts: the main functions, UI interface, 2D, virtual model, materials, and model and editor.  
Let me explain the first three parts.  

The first is the main function.  
In the new version Claude 7.3, the main function to mention is the fabric generator.  
We can easily generate fabric based on the input of actual fabric information.  
We can also use the preview window to see the model results.  
Now let's see how to use this function.  
We can open the fabric generator in two ways.  
First, select the material in the main menu.  
Second, select the editor.  
Third, select the fabric generator.  
The fabric generator will appear in the preview window at the same time as the new default material is added to the preview window.  
Another way to open it is to right-click on the existing fabric in the preview window and select the fabric generator.  
If you want to apply it to the clothing when creating the fabric,  
or you want to use the fabric generator to recreate the fabric already applied to the clothing, you can use it.  

Next, let me introduce the window interface of the fabric generator.  
It is mainly divided into two windows.  
The window below allows you to enter the fabric information you want to generate,  
and select the type of fabric, ingredients, and the percentage of input ingredients.  
Then enter the weight and set the texture of the fabric to be generated.  
In the preview window above, you can open the results in 3D according to the input information.  
By default, the preview window can be opened.  
You can select the size and shape of the fabric,  
and you can change the preview window to the desired view by selecting the preview window in the upper right corner.  
You can also use the mouse to move the screen to define the view.  
After adjusting the view, you can click the lock icon in the upper right corner to fix the view you have adjusted.  

In the model selection in the upper left corner,  
you can select the round shape, flat shape, and square shape.  
Currently, the diameter is 30 cm, and the round shape is placed on the round shape.  
Through this pull-down list, we can select the flat shape.  
We can see that the fabric is flat on the human model as a flat shape.  
The square round shape can be seen as a 30 cm x 30 cm square object placed over the round shape.  

Next, we will operate on how to use the fabric generator.  
First, fill in the information of the fabric,  
enter the name of the fabric,  
the supplier, and all users,  
and then select the fabric type and ingredients to be generated.  
The fabric type here provides 63 types of fabric,  
and you can select the fabric type according to your needs.  
The ingredient options for different fabric types will also change.  
Therefore, we select the fabric type and the corresponding ingredients at the same time,  
enter the percentage of the ingredients,  
and then enter the weight.  
You can edit the model result in the show window based on the actual input.  

Now let's start setting up the fabric structure.  
There are three ways to set up the fabric structure in the fabric generator.  
The first way  
is that if we have a suitable sticker structure,  
we can manually add patterns to define the fabric material we need to improve its performance.  
If you don't have a suitable sticker, you can use the Closed preview texture.  
Open the Closed preview texture to see the texture options that match the selected material type.  
Then select and download the texture you want.  
After downloading, click on it to apply to the material.  
You can check the effect in the preview window.  

The last method:  
On the right side of the texture sticker, there is a model icon.  
Click it.  
Open the window of the AI texture generator.  
You can use it to generate and apply the texture.  
The detailed operation method of the AI texture generator will be discussed later.  

After setting up the material type and texture,  
if you need to make detailed adjustments to the physical properties of the material,  
you can click on the detail option on the left side of the small handle.  

Before the new version of Cloud 7.3,  
it used 16 parameters to represent the physical properties of the plant.  
However, in the material generator,  
we use the same method,  
with 4 additional parameters called growth rate added on the original parameter base.  
To represent the physical properties of the parameters,  
the total number reaches 20.  

So, the physical properties of the Closed material are now divided into V1 and V2.  
V1 is the data measured by the current material measurement.  
V2 is the material data created by our material generator.  
In V2, with the improvement of the non-linear stretching implementation method,  
it allows the use of linear variables for more detailed control.  

The physical properties of the raw material may differ from the original material details, so please be careful when making such changes.  
If you want to redo it after modifying the details, you can click the arrow button in the upper right corner.  

After the material is generated, click the apply button below.  
In the material generator, the input information will be updated in the material attribute editor.  
At the same time, this material will be applied to 3D clothing.  
All you need to do is click the model key in the 3D window to check the condition of the clothing.  
Please remember that the result displayed in the 3D window is based on the data generated by the test fit.  
In order to accurately reflect the physical properties of the material, the test fit model must be used.  
When you click apply and close, the attribute of the material will be applied to the clothing and the material generator window will be closed simultaneously.  

To store the raw material in the ZFAB format, click the save button in the lower left corner.  
If you just want to adjust the physical properties of the material, you can click the details in the physical properties menu of the attribute editor.  
Click the arrow button in the upper right corner.  
Click the material generator details window to adjust the value.  
You can adjust the value by clicking the button in the upper right corner.  
Click the arrow button in the upper right corner.  
Click the arrow button to adjust the value by clicking the button in the upper left corner.  
You can adjust the value by field and then click the package window to check the qualitative performance.  

Let's talk about material version questions.  
As mentioned above, the material generator has added and uses a new parameter called growth rate.  
The original parameter-class material stored in the previous version, 7.3,  
has been marked as V1, including the volume of the new parameter.  
Select the material and then check the information in the attribute editor.  
The physical attribute is difficult to check.  
If the material is version 1, it will be displayed as V1.  
Version 2 is displayed as V2.  

For more detailed information,  
you can click the triangle icon on the left.  
Then the output is divided into the creator and the data state.  
In the creator menu,  
you can check the creation method of the material:  
whether it is default material,  
material calculated, or material generated by the material generator  
can be displayed here.  

In the data state column,  
you can check whether the physical properties of the material have been changed.  
If the detailed information has not been changed, it is original.  
If changed, it will be edited.  

The material generator can use three types of materials:  
In Cloud 7.3 or higher versions,  
use the material created by the increase button on the roof window.  
The second is in the material generator, use V2.3 for all materials necessary for production.  
The third is to convert from V1 to V2.  

How to convert V2 from V1:  
Materials stored in versions before Cloud 7.3  
cannot be used in the material generator  
because of the lack of related data,  
one of the growth rate parameters introduced in V2.  

So, when opening them with the material generator,  
a warning window that cannot be read in the material generator will appear.  
For materials produced before version 7.3,  
if there is data that uses the same measurement, it can be converted to V2.  
When there is measurement data in the ZFAB, the physical attribute will be displayed as the measurement calculation.  

Convert V1 to V2:  
First, select V1 in the physical window.  
In the physical editor, the physical attribute on the right side will show a conversion icon.  
If the material does not have measurement data, it will not display the conversion icon.  
Click on Convert.  
You will notice that the physical attribute in the attribute editor changes from V1 to V2.  

If you want to check the material simulation effect stored in Cloud 7.3,  
or want to use the material generator to predict rather than simulate,  
or want to add growth rate parameters to the material and make detailed adjustments,  
you need to convert V1 to V2.  

The original material in Cloud 7.3 can be converted to V2 and then used in the material generator, because they have measurement data.  
In addition, to make it easier for users to use V2 material and the material generator to perform various tasks,  
the material preset has also been updated.  
You can see about 190 V2 materials have been added to Cloud 7.3.  
If you want to use V2 material, click the download button in the upper right corner of Cloud 7.3.  

The second main function to be introduced is the AI physics generator.  
By setting and inputting keywords,  
the physics of the generated material with the required pattern is displayed.  
In addition, you can also check the generated pattern on 3D clothing.  
Currently, the AI physics generator has been tested as a test service,  
and is only open to pre-registered test personnel.  
After Cloud 7.3 version,  
the selected test personnel can use the function for one month.  
After feedback from test personnel has been improved,  
we plan to soon allow all users to use the official version.  

The newly added content will be released on the Cloud website.  
To ensure good test progress,  
the number of AI physics generators is limited.  
If you generate one, the AI physics generator will deduct the remaining number.  

Now let's take a closer look.  
First, in the object window,  
select the AI physics material to be generated.  
Click on the AI physics generator on the right side of the attribute editor.  
At this time, if the selected material is applied to the clothing,  
you can immediately check the AI physics generator in the 3D window  
to generate the material physics effect.  

In addition, when we generate the material in the material generator,  
we can also open the AI physics generator.  
Let's open the material generator.  
Click on the model icon on the right side of the texture sticker.  
The AI physics generator will be generated directly in the material generator.  

Next, let's take a look at the operation window of the AI physics generator.  
In this window,  
you can set multiple options  
and enter the keyword in the keyword prompt to generate the required material.  
The window below will display an AI physics pattern after generation.  
If you click on the history record on the right side,  
you will see the history record window.  
You can check the previously generated physics pattern here again.  
You can also check the generated pattern and preceding patterns.  
The option is the type you want to enter, and the keyword input.  
The history record will only keep the clear action off.  
If you need to save the physics,  

Let's look at the setting of options before creating AI physics.  
We can choose about 3 categories of options.  
The first one is the dough type.  
Click on the dough type dropdown menu.  
After selecting, it will generate a texture pattern on the corresponding surface texture.  
If you select a circle, it will generate a texture pattern on the surface texture, and if you select a circle, it will not activate the start generation button, so you must select it.  
Now I choose the flat pattern type.  

The second is the pattern type.  
There are three options here: no style, style, and pattern.  
Style and pattern here are translation issues, which will be improved later.  
Effectively generate the pattern texture you want through these three types.  
After selecting the pattern type, enter the keyword of the texture in the input texture.  
You can generate the desired result.  

Let's first go through a PPT to understand the various pattern types.  
After entering the keyword hint, what kind of AI texture image is generated?  
If the pattern type chooses style, you can choose cartoon, watercolor, sketch, oil painting, and copy these options, and create a corresponding texture image.  
If you choose the pattern type as pattern, you can select color pattern, Socrates pattern, Pellis pattern, dot and line pattern.  

Next, let's take a look at how to set these options specifically.  
If you want to set a specific style,  
you can add a style to the AI texture image you want to generate.  
After choosing the style, a submenu will appear below.  
You can choose a specific style from it.  
This way, you can apply the characteristics of the style to the AI texture image.  
If you want to generate an AI texture image that is a single loop pattern,  
select the pattern type.  
Then select the desired pattern through the submenu at the bottom.  
Apply the characteristics of the pattern to the AI texture image.  

If the AI texture image you want to generate is not affected by any pattern type,  
and you only want to generate it through the material type and keyword,  
you can select no pattern type.  

Through the pattern size, the size of a loop pattern can be adjusted to four levels.  
When choosing the material and pattern type, the pattern size defaults to 1.  
If the pattern size is set to 1, it will generate nearly 1024 pixels randomly.  
If the pattern size is set to 4,  
it will generate nearly 4096 pixels randomly,  
which is 4 times the size of 1024 pixels.  

Next, enter the keyword.  
Note that the current text can only be entered in English.  
After entering the prompt, the button to start generation becomes active.  
When creating a generated AI pattern,  
the left number is deducted.  
During the generation process, you can see the server prompt and progress.  
After the AI pattern is generated,  
click on apply,  
apply the object to 3D clothing,  
and you can see the result in advance.  

When entering the keyword,  
it is recommended to enter words,  
not long texts.  
Long texts may lead to missing images.  
Therefore, use dots or control grids to divide the words.  
Finally, click on start generation to see the result.  

If you want to highlight some characteristics of the word,  
you can add a keyword weight.  
When using the keyword,  
use it once to emphasize 1.1 times.  
Use it twice to emphasize 1.1 squared times.  
For example, when entering "yellow sky" and adding weight,  
you can see that the generated image result adds more weight with the increase of the keyword.  

In the lower right corner of the keyword prompt,  
there is a flash-shaped icon.  
Its function is to maintain the material type and pattern size of the previous setting unchanged.  
You can select the pattern type and keyword prompt randomly,  
and generate different types of text and applications this way.  

The function of the real-type icon is  
to generate similar text patterns while maintaining the existing pattern.  
Because even if you enter the same prompt,  
different text results will be generated each time.  
If you want to keep the style of the existing text pattern as much as possible,  
you can click on the real-type icon.  
Hovering the mouse over the real-type icon will display the tool prompt.  
As described in the tool prompt,  
by clicking it,  
you can generate a new pattern similar to the previously generated text pattern.  
Remember, if the results are different,  
the details still depend on the prompt added or modified.  

In addition, the AI text generator window can be minimized.  
When many users generate text at the same time,  
it takes some time to complete.  
If the waiting time is longer,  
you can minimize the window by clicking the arrow in the upper right corner.  
Once the material is generated,  
the text prompt will be updated  
to achieve effective use of the software.  

Next, the last main function I want to introduce is link editing.  
From version 7.3,  
we can simultaneously edit the link lines in the pattern,  
thereby improving work efficiency.  
Not only the outer outline or inner line of the pattern,  
but also the sewing line can be adjusted at the same time.  
This function consists of link lines and editing link tools.  
The link tool will set the link to the selected part of the line.  
The editing link tool will change the link line according to the selected option.  

Next, we will show you how to set the selected line as a link  
through the link tool and how to edit the link line through the link editing function.  

Next, let's see how to operate a series of operations on the Jack board.  
Select the edit board tool from the 2D toolbar,  
then select the line to be set as the link line.  
Right-click on the line,  
and find the link line at the bottom of the list.  
When you click on the link line,  
the selected line will be displayed in blue.  
When we hover the mouse  
on the outer outline of the pattern to be set as the link,  
it will display two lines with an empty line,  
and they will be linked.  
At this time, the setting direction of the link line depends on the selected direction.  
This is similar to the setting direction of the sewing line.  
Therefore, it is necessary to maintain  
that the two lines are parallel to each other.  

In addition, if you want to connect one whole line to multiple lines,  
press the Shift key on the keyboard,  
and select multiple lines to be linked.  
You can see that two lines are linked to one line.  
After clicking on the line,  
you can see that the linked lines are connected through the sewing line,  
and there are double-line arrows at the center of the sewing line.  
If you select the empty area in the second window,  
the sewing line of the linked line will be hidden.  
You can click on the line again to display the empty line,  
to check whether they are linked.  

Select the Edit sewing line tool,  
select the line with teeth below,  
and show that the lines here have been sewed.  
You can use the Edit sewing line tool to quickly link the lines.  
On the sewing line, right-click and select Link Line.  
You can see that the sewed lines have been linked.  

In the state of selecting the Edit sewing line tool,  
right-click and select Link Line.  
Click on Unlink to cancel the link.  
Remember, if you delete the sewing line directly from the link line,  
the link line will be automatically removed.  

After the link line is set,  
select the Edit sewing line tool,  
and select two lines on the edit sewing line,  
and drag them down.  
As you can see,  
the linked line with teeth is also modified.  
Similarly, the line with teeth is moved up and down,  
and the line with teeth is moved up and down.  
When the line with teeth is moved up and down,  
the line with teeth is also changed.  
When selecting the point to modify,  
only the point on the linked line will be modified together.  
The point on the linked line will remain unchanged.  

Come to the sewing line,  
and set the sewing line to Link.  
Note that the length of the two linked lines here is different.  
At this time, you can use the Edit sewing line tool  
to check the edit sewing line.  
Select Edit sewing line,  
press and move the point of the linked line,  
and you can modify the length of the linked line.  

On the linked line,  
right-click and select the three editing options.  
Let's take a look at each option.  
The first one is to remove the linked line.  
The button can remove the linked line.  
The second one is to turn the direction.  
The button can change the direction of the linked line.  
At this time, there is only one arrow direction on the sewing line,  
and it is used to distinguish the direction of the linked line.  
When displaying a single arrow,  
the linked line will move in the same direction.  
When displaying a double arrow,  
it will move in the opposite direction.  
In addition, the turning direction can also be set in the attribute editor on the right side.  

The last option is to add a sewing line to the linked line.  
Only when the linked line is not sewed,  
can this option be seen.  
You can automatically sew the linked line through the button.  

After the pocket and side seams are all modified,  
simulate and check the modified results in the 3D window.  

In addition to the linked line length with the editing link tool mentioned earlier,  
you can also add a straight line on the line and then link the part lines.  

Using this method,  
the linked line will be linked to the hanging line,  
and the linked line will be modified.  

In addition,  
all lines can be automatically generated and linked  
when using the hook and loop tool to create a board.  

First,  
create the inner line of the pocket at the front chest of the clip,  
select the hook and loop tool,  
select the pocket line,  
and click the right button on the line to see the option of connecting the hook as a board.  
Click it,  
and the hooked board will be displayed.  

After placing the 2D board in the blank area,  
you can see that the pocket and the large board are linked.  
The pocket and the large board are completely linked.  

Then,  
use the editing link tool to add the linked line.  
After adding the linked line,  
add the board to the outside.  
Use the editing board tool to modify the pocket board.  
You can try to check the effect in the 3D window.  

In addition,  
when the length of the linked line changes,  
the length of the linked line will also automatically match the length.  

After modifying,  
you can use the editing link tool to remove the linked line.  

The best way to use this function is  
to organize the deck board according to the previous order,  
and to simulate the floating board.  

After the shape of the clothing is simulated,  
select multiple floating lines and set them as linked lines.  
This way, you can edit the linked lines and use them at the same time.  
By following this procedure,  
you can greatly simplify the setting process.  

The following is the introduction of the UI interface.  

Next,  
we will talk about the update and improvement of the Closet in the Closet software.  
To use the Closet database and Closet data more easily,  
we have improved four functions in version 7.3.  
Let's take a look at them one by one.  

First,  
we have updated the Closet spreadsheet.  
In the previous version,  
when the Closet and Connect in the Closet window are downloaded,  
the preview image of the project will be displayed.  
The preview image of the project is not displayed when the file is saved.  
Now,  
when the function is updated,  
whether it is downloaded or not,  
the preview image will always be displayed.  

For example,  
in the previous version,  
in the Closet Connect,  
after downloading some projects such as the chain or the button,  
the preview image will be immediately changed.  
When we try to check them again,  
the preview image and the preview image will be confused.  

Through the improvement of this function,  
even if we choose and download the previous one,  
the preview image will be displayed.  
The preview image will also be displayed as a screenshot,  
to reduce confusion.  

Secondly,  
a new folder named All Contents has been added to the Closet.  
In the past,  
to search for a certain file,  
we had to enter the collection content or the required company database,  
and search for the project name.  
Through this improvement,  
we can directly select All Contents,  
and search for the required project name,  
which will display all the projects with that name.  

Thirdly,  
the search-related functions have been improved.  
Before version 7.3,  
the file information in the folder was searched,  
but from this version,  
the information in the Closet has been changed to search.  
In the past,  
when searching for a keyword,  
if there was no result,  
there would not be a single prompt message,  
but from the new version,  
it will clearly display a prompt that there is no search result,  
so that you can more intuitively  
check whether the current search can be completed.  

Next is the final improvement.  
Before version 7.3,  
when selecting the file from the library,  
such as the T2M copy file,  
you needed to download it first,  
add it to the object window,  
and drag it to the 3D window board,  
or directly download it to copy and drag it to the board.  

From version 7.3,  
after selecting the file,  
you can drag it directly to the board corresponding to the 3D window,  
and then download it.  
This reduces operation time.  

Next,  
I will introduce the improvement of the color version UI interface.  
In the previous version,  
even if the color block in the custom color version does not exist,  
it will be saved.  
But if you open the custom color version file again,  
you will not be able to load the color block because the color block does not exist.  
No file is loaded,  
so the file is not loaded.  

From version 7.3,  
the custom color version has been improved  
to avoid this issue.  
In the custom color version,  
if there is no color block,  
click Save.  
To find the color,  
please add a color to save the file in the view window.  
When adding a color block with no color block,  
this view window will also appear.  

Next,  
I will introduce the improvement of the display or hidden layer color function.  
From the beginning of the version,  
the layer has been improved.  
The color that can be displayed or hidden layer  
is the same as the frozen hardening and shape optimization.  

First,  
we set a layer in the pattern.  
Select the pattern you want to set the layer,  
and come to the attribute editor.  
Set the layer value to 1.  
We can see in the 3D window that  
the color of the selected pattern has changed to light green.  

To hide the layer color of the pattern,  
right-click on the background of the 3D window,  
select the hidden layer from the display or hidden color menu,  
and the light green of the pattern will be hidden.  

If you want to display the color again,  
you can do the same in the 3D window,  
right-click on the background,  
and select the display layer from the display or hidden color menu.  

The last UI improvement function to be introduced is the increase of setting and shrinkage of the ZSE scene file when saving the ZSE scene file.  
From the beginning of the version,  
we can add another ZSE image when saving the scene file.  
In the past,  
when saving the scene file,  
there was no separate ZSE image file,  
and only the name of the saved image was displayed.  

From version 7.3,  
we can register and save the ZSE image,  
so that we can check the ZSE image in the cloud library.  

Next,  
let's save the file as a scene file  
and check it in the cloud library.  
In the main menu,  
select File and save it as a scene tool.  
In the saved scene and tool window,  
we can register the ZSE image in it.  

There are two options in the window:  
automatic and user-defined.  
When set to automatic,  
the screen front image that is currently visible in the 3D window  
will be automatically saved as a ZSE image.  

When selecting the user-defined option,  
a plus frame will appear at the bottom.  
Click on the image that you select to be registered as a ZSE image on the computer.  
After selecting the image,  
click Open.  

The ZSE image shown in the frame can be displayed.  
Click Confirm.  
Select the path to store the scene file.  
You can save the scene file and the ZSE image together.  

In the library,  
we find the ZSE scene file just saved.  
When we hover the mouse  
on the file,  
it will display the file’s custom information.  

Next is the update and improvement of the 2D function.  

First, I will introduce the improvement of the edit function.  
In the previous version, if the length of the border line is different,  
we must remember the length of one of the lines,  
and use the modify length function to directly connect the length to fix it.  

Now, the new 7.3 function can easily modify the length of the line to the specified length.  
Let's use this function to modify the linked group of two lines with different lengths due to the border line.  

Select the edit file tool,  
press the Shift key on the keyboard,  
and select the two lines on the border line.  
You can see that  
the length of the two lines is different,  
646.9 mm and 604.8 mm respectively.  

Then in this state,  
right-click on the line,  
select Copy from the pop-up menu,  
correct the length,  
and then select the correct length window.  

Next, let's take a look at each setting option of the window.  
The first is matching.  
You can set it to choose which line length to modify,  
and select the shorter one to be modified  
to see the length of the two lines in data form.  

Find a longer line to be modified to the shorter line.  
And the line will display an arrow,  
and the measurement value below will display the length of the short line.  

When selecting the length,  
you will see the length of the shorter line modified to the longer line in the 2D window,  
and the measurement value will also display the length of the longer line.  

The second direction is the direction of the set line length to be reduced or increased.  
The operation principle is the same as the length change.  
If you choose Start, the length of the line will change from the starting point of the line.  
The direction of the change is indicated by the yellow arrow at the end of the line where the change occurs.  

If you choose Center, the length will change from the center of the line and the arrow will appear in two directions.  
When the selection is over, the length changes from the end point and the yellow arrow will appear in the direction of the change.  

Here we choose Start and click OK.  
We can immediately check the modification in the 2D window and click to simulate.  
In the 3D window, you can see that the side seam has disappeared.  
It can be used to modify the side seam line connected to the seam line.  
It can also be easily used for two-layer panels, such as collar panels.  

Even if the panel is lined with multiple layers, it can also use the correct length function.  
This type of E0 panel, we found that it is lined with two layers using the cloning function.

chunks.content: # CLO 7.3 New Features and Comprehensive Updates This document details the new features, UI improvements, 2D and 3D enhancements, virtual model updates, material advancements, and editor optimizations introduced in CLO version 7.3. It focuses on technical explanations, procedures, parameter specifications, and practical examples relevant to users upgrading their design experience. --- ## Main Functions Overview: Fabric Generator, AI Physics Generator, and Link Editing This section covers the core new functionalities in CLO 7.3, including the fabric generator for creating realistic fabric textures from input data, the AI physics generator for AI-assisted material physics and texture creation, and enhanced link editing for pattern line management. ### Fabric Generator **Overview:** The fabric generator enables users to create fabric textures based on actual fabric data inputs, preview the results in 3D, and fine-tune physical properties with extended parameters. **Accessing the Fabric Generator:** - Via the main menu under Material > Fabric Generator - Through the Editor > Fabric Generator - Right-clicking an existing fabric in the preview window and selecting Fabric Generator When opened, a new default material is added to the preview window alongside the fabric generator interface. **Interface Structure:** - **Lower window:** Input fabric information, including fabric name, supplier, fabric type, ingredients (with adjustable percentages), weight, and texture settings. - **Upper Preview window:** Displays 3D visualization of the generated fabric according to input parameters. Users can select fabric shape (round, flat, square), size (default diameter 30 cm), and control the camera view with mouse interaction and a lock icon. **Fabric Shapes:** - Round Shape (default 30 cm diameter placed on a round base) - Flat Shape (fabric displayed flat on a human model) - Square Shape (30 cm x 30 cm square fabric placed over a round base) **Fabric Setup Process:** 1. Enter fabric metadata: name, supplier, user info. 2. Select from 63 fabric types; ingredient options dynamically update accordingly. 3. Specify ingredient percentages and fabric weight. 4. Adjust fabric structure via one of three methods: - Manually add sticker patterns if available. - Use Closed preview textures to select and download matching material textures. - Use the AI texture generator (accessed via the model icon next to texture sticker) for AI-generated textures. **Physical Property Adjustments:** - Access detailed physical properties via the detail option on the left handle. - Previous CLO versions used 16 parameters; version 7.3 adds 4 growth rate parameters, totaling 20 parameters for fabric physical properties. - Two versions of fabric physical data: - **V1:** Measured data from current materials. - **V2:** Data generated by the material generator, supporting improved non-linear stretching and linear variable control. - Caution: Raw material physical properties may differ from originals; modifications should be done carefully. - Undo changes with the arrow button in the upper right corner. **Applying and Saving Materials:** - Click **Apply** to update material attributes and apply them to 3D clothing. - Use the model key in the 3D window to check fit and fabric behavior (requires test fit model for accuracy).

chunks.content: - **V2:** Data generated by the material generator, supporting improved non-linear stretching and linear variable control. - Caution: Raw material physical properties may differ from originals; modifications should be done carefully. - Undo changes with the arrow button in the upper right corner. **Applying and Saving Materials:** - Click **Apply** to update material attributes and apply them to 3D clothing. - Use the model key in the 3D window to check fit and fabric behavior (requires test fit model for accuracy). - Save raw material data in **ZFAB** format using the save button at the lower left. - Physical properties can be further adjusted via the physical properties menu in the attribute editor. **Material Versioning and Conversion:** - CLO 7.3 introduces growth rate parameters in V2 materials. - Materials from previous versions (V1) lack these parameters and cannot be directly used in the material generator. - Conversion from V1 to V2 is possible if measurement data exists: - Select V1 physical data in the editor; a conversion icon appears if conversion is possible. - Click **Convert** to update to V2. - Over 190 V2 materials are available in CLO 7.3 and can be downloaded via the download button. - Material creator and data state can be checked by expanding details in the attribute editor, showing whether materials are default, calculated, or generated, and if physical properties have been edited. --- ### AI Physics Generator **Overview:** The AI physics generator uses keyword input to generate material physics patterns and textures, previewable on 3D clothing. Currently in test service, it is limited to pre-registered users for one month, with plans for full release after feedback improvements. **Accessing the AI Physics Generator:** - Select a material in the object window and click **AI physics generator** in the attribute editor. - Alternatively, open it from the material generator via the model icon next to the texture sticker. **Operation Window Features:** - Multiple options and keyword input prompt to generate specific materials. - History record panel to review previously generated patterns. - Options include dough type, pattern type, pattern size, and keyword prompt input. **Option Categories:** - **Dough Type:** Choose surface texture type; required to activate generation. - **Pattern Type:** Three options: no style, style, and pattern. - *Style* applies artistic styles (cartoon, watercolor, sketch, oil painting). - *Pattern* applies structural patterns (color pattern, Socrates pattern, Pellis pattern, dot and line patterns). - *No pattern* generates texture based on material type and keyword alone. - **Pattern Size:** Four levels (1 to 4), controlling resolution from ~1024 pixels (size 1) up to ~4096 pixels (size 4). **Keyword Input:** - English text only. - Short words recommended; avoid long sentences to prevent missing image results. - Keyword weighting: repeated keywords emphasize certain characteristics exponentially (e.g., repeated twice = 1.1² times emphasis). **Icons:** - **Flash icon:** Keeps material type and pattern size fixed, allowing random pattern and keyword variation. - **Real-type icon:** Generates similar patterns maintaining style despite prompt variations.
